traits.leaf_length_m.note: Jepson (1925), as O. cerasiformis: leaves 3.8 cm to 6.3 cm long (converted from inches).

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944), as Osmaronia cerasiformis: a shrub or small tree 1 m to 5 m high.

traits.juvenile_period_years.note: The Woody Plant Seed Manual (Oemleria chapter, text, read): first flowering occurred 2 years after germination on male plants raised from seed (no figure given for female, fruit-bearing plants).

generator.params.spur_leaf.note: A short shoot's leaf card, a little smaller than a long shoot's (leaf_size), within Jepson (1925): leaves 3.8 to 6.3 cm long.

generator.params.leaf_size.note: Leaf card length, petiole included, sized so every leaf drawn stays within Jepson (1925, as O. cerasiformis): leaves 1.5 to 2.5 in (3.8 to 6.3 cm) long (0.12 drew them 10 to 11 cm).

traits.flowering_months.note: iNaturalist research-grade records on GBIF in the south and central Puget Sound lowlands (46.7 to 48.0° N, 122.0 to 123.1° W; counted 2026-10-14): 602 records annotated as flowering (Jan 13, Feb 113, Mar 344, Apr 132); stated as the months holding at least a tenth of them, February to April. The Seed Manual (Oemleria chapter, printed p. 750) gives January to May, with latitude and elevation.

traits.fruiting_months.note: USA National Phenology Network observations (Nature's Notebook) at lowland sites west of the Cascades in Washington and Oregon (below 300 m, west of 121.8° W; 2009 to 2026, fetched 2026-10-14): 30 plant-years at 10 sites seen with ripe fruit, by the months they were seen in (Apr 1, May 5, Jun 19, Jul 10, Aug 3, Sep 2, Oct 1); stated as the months with at least a third as many as the busiest, June and July. Seed Manual, Oemleria chapter (printed p. 750): ripe by early summer, and in the Pacific Northwest birds and mammals take the fruit from May to July; so ripe fruit is on the plant from May to July.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a tall, upright shrub of slender stems with narrow, light green leaves and hanging racemes of white bell flowers; the first shrub to leaf out in late winter. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 3.2 m tall at 12 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: light green leaves; white hanging flowers; purple-brown bark. Fruit (plant roadmap P4), as in mid-July: short hanging racemes of plum-like drupes, orange ripening blue-black. Its year (appearance.organs.bloom.season) takes its days of bud, flower, fruit, ripe and fall from the months it flowers and fruits in, by the rules at the flowering plants (development, 2026-10-14); until then they were authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands: hanging white racemes in February and March; fruit orange, then blue-black from June, gone by August. The forest's packages show day 196 (mid-July) until the phenology of plant roadmap P5 sets the day from the date and the local climate. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): smooth purplish-brown bark with lenticels; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

appearance.organs.bloom.season.flower_lo.note: Its flowers drawn one by one (spec rework L1b): greenish-white bell-like flowers 1 to 1.5 cm across with 15 stamens, in hanging racemes that open from the base. From general descriptions of the species (OregonFlora, the Flora of North America and nursery and extension pages as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read). The size is the flower's width, or a closed corolla's length, over the fruit's length, roughly as in life. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): five greenish-white petals between five sepals on a floral cup, fifteen stamens and five free pistils, from the characters of Rosaceae and Oemleria by the rules at the flowering plants.

appearance.organs.bloom.season.opening.note: Days from the first flower of a cluster opening to its last: a third of the days from its first flower to its first fruit as they were set by hand before 2026-10-14, a convention (no source gives a raceme's opening time).
